results.content:
Subscribed.fyi on its Dorik review page under 'Cons' summarized recurring complaints about limited integrations, occasional instability, and missing multilingual support. The report said some users experienced glitches and wished for stronger e-commerce features. It highlighted export and integration limits behind higher tiers and advised teams requiring advanced commerce or localization to validate feature coverage before adopting Dorik for production workloads and to ask support about roadmap commitments and SLAs directly.

## Dorik AI Pricing

### Dorik AI — Pricing & Plans (updated September 24, 2025) [...] Capterra reviewer under the thread titled 'Falsely Advertised a Free Plan' alleged Dorik switched from a free tier to a trial without clear notice. The user said repeated contacts with sales led to circular responses and a push toward paid yearly offers. Complaints emphasized time lost reconstructing work and distrust about billing practices. The reviewer urged potential users to confirm plan limits and retention policies before relying on the platform. [...] Aude D-VES on Trustpilot (insight.dorik.io) in the thread 'CMS , SEO DO NOT WORK AT ALL ON DORIK' reported prolonged CMS failures over several months. The user alleged repeated video calls and messages failed to resolve publishing and data loss problems. They claimed SEO features were ineffective and that ongoing bugs made the paid service unusable. The complaint urged others to consider more reliable options until issues are fixed completely.

results.content:
Shubham Pratap Singh

#### What's great

Dorik has been the easiest website builder I’ve used. The templates look clean, the editor is simple to work with, and I was able to get a site live much faster than with other tools. The CMS is straightforward, and support has been great whenever I needed help. I’d love a bit more flexibility in some design tweaks, but overall it’s a smooth, hassle-free experience. Highly recommend for anyone who wants to build quickly without overthinking the tech.

Lakshya Singh

#### What's great

This is really good! Its fast, creative and on-point. I love that it gives you that chatgpt kind of response - like you watch it create a website, it scrolls while doing it. The images it used looks good and the color combinations are amazing! Totally recommended! [...] #### What needs improvement

The only drawback I can see is the annoying "feedback" button on the left that looks like it blocks some options (it doesn't though) and that there are too many options to edit. But I really didn't need to give it anything except for the prompt.

Carlos Justino

#### What's great

Very easy to use.  
The interface is clear and intuitive.  
I built and published quickly without friction.  
The no-code builder is flexible and well designed.  
Performance is fast and reliable.  
Pricing feels fair for the value delivered.  
Overall, a solid and trustworthy product.

#### What needs improvement

Custom domain setup can be clearer.  
More stability during peak times would help.

#### vs Alternatives

Replit [...] Pricing remains a killer advantage—super affordable plans starting low, way better value than Webflow or Squarespace for most non-enterprise use cases. Performance is snappy, SEO basics are covered out of the box, and the overall experience is lightweight and modern.

That said, it's not perfect for everything: e-commerce is still pretty basic (simple cart + payment buttons, but nothing like Shopify-level depth), so scaling a full online store might require moving elsewhere later. Template variety is decent but not massive—if you have super-niche design needs, you'll tweak more. A few users mention occasional minor bugs, but support is generally responsive and the platform keeps improving steadily.

## Dorik website builder review: Summary

Dorik is an affordable and easy-to-use website builder that competes with the likes of B12 and Durable. While it doesn’t break enough new ground to set itself apart, it gets the basics right and has reasonable pricing plans that don’t break the bank. We like it for its useful export feature, a decent component library, and dedicated site management and collaboration tools.

However, Dorik struggles with advanced customization and its no-code builder can be a bit slow to respond at times. While it doesn’t exactly impede work, the editor’s initial loading time and overall lagging issues can be a bit of a downer.

Ritoban Mukherjee

Ritoban Mukherjee

Contributing Writer - Software [...] (Image credit: © Dorik)

### TechRadar Verdict

Dorik is a relatively new AI website builder that launched in 2020. While its AI features are still in beta, it gets the core basics right. We’d have appreciated more customization options, however.

#### Pros

 +

  User-friendly drag-and-drop interface
 +

  Responsive design for all devices
 +

  AI-powered site generation

#### Cons

 -

  Occasional bugs and downtime
 -

  Limited granular design control
 -

  Not enough template variety
